outcome: time of initial mobility after surgery
cohort: The study included 206 pregnant women aged 15-50 years undergoing Cesarean section delivery in Basra Teaching Hospital, Basra, Iraq.
finding: Increased maternal BMI was significantly correlated with higher rates of maternal complications (gestational hypertension, GDM, longer duration of surgery and hospital stay, delayed initial mobility, intestinal sounds, and breastfeeding) and neonatal complications (macrosomia, NICU admission) among women undergoing C-section.
